errors: Re-measures per group of changes rather than per change, so gains cannot be attributed
Offers a small VPS as a hosting option without noting the admin burden or migration risk
R4-A.why: Broad, well ordered and grounded with numeric targets, cache exclusions, cart fragments and a TTFB branch; weaker on change discipline (no one-at-a-time, off-peak or explicit rollback) and on migration risk.

errors: Third-party scripts (pixels, chat, reviews) are not addressed
R4-B.why: Measurement-led with runnable commands, a per-change revert rule, concrete cache-leak and checkout checks, and a gated hosting move with preconditions and rollback; only gap is third-party scripts.

R4-C.why: Tight, safe and proportionate: server/browser split, cart-leak test, single cache plugin, trial-clone hosting decision and explicit deferrals; numeric targets are postponed and database work is thin.

errors: Freezing product edits during the DNS switch does not by itself prevent orders being split between hosts
No mention of the 28-day field-data lag or ongoing re-checks
R4-D.why: Catches every trap with concrete actions and checks (cookie-level cache bypass, cached vs uncached TTFB, gated hosting and theme branches, per-change revert) and flags the uncached cart/checkout path up front.

errors: No numeric targets stated; deferred entirely to after baseline
R4-E.why: Sound measure-then-fix plan with a strong cache go/no-go, plugin approval rule and quiet-hour changes; lacks numeric targets and a warning on JS optimisation, and is less specific than the top three.

errors: Unsupported claim that Phase 1 typically takes 6 s to 2.5-3.5 s
Query Monitor install not tied to staging
No per-change checkout test or rollback step; business-critical plugins not protected
R4-F.why: Comprehensive and technically correct checklist with targets and cache exclusions, but it does not branch on the TTFB result and is thin on live-store safety: no one-change-at-a-time, purchase test or undo path.

errors: Relies on cache plugins excluding WooCommerce pages by default instead of verifying as a step (covered only in Risks)
Migration described as a day or two with no cutover or rollback plan
R4-G.why: Concise, correctly ordered from cheap to disruptive with targets, per-change re-measurement and a useful risk list; hosting migration and rollback are under-specified and critical plugins are not named for protection.

errors: States shared hosting is 'very likely too small' and that it would move, largely pre-judging the hosting decision before data
No warning on JS/CSS deferral breaking checkout; no rollback step
Small VPS offered without admin caveat
R4-H.why: Short and sensibly ordered with the right cache exclusions, but hosting is half-assumed, the baseline is light on metrics, and change control on the live store is limited to retesting checkout.
